text:
Samir: Heads-up — saw sustained queue growth in us-west-2 hot-reserve this morning, admission started rejecting at ~72% GPU util.
Priya: Which queue? user-facing? batch?
Samir: Front-tier gen (low-latency). spike around 10:12 UTC after a traffic burst from a marketing campaign.
Jorge: Any network blips? we've seen egress queueing make pods slow and autoscaler overshoot in the past.
Samir: Network graphs show 200ms tail on pod attach during the spike. kube-probe flapping at the same time.
Leah: If attach latency is the culprit, autoscaler sees pods not ready and keeps scaling, but admission fills the new capacity. Sounds like a feedback loop.
Priya: So we can: raise soft-admit threshold, reserve a small standby buffer per AZ, or lengthen autoscaler cooldown to avoid overshoot. Tradeoffs: cost vs tail latency.
Jorge: Also consider smarter admission: short-lived soft-deny with backoff keyed by client id, not a hard reject. That reduces user retries.
Samir: Quick config idea (for canary):
```yaml
front_tier:
  soft_admit: 0.65
  standby_nodes_per_az: 3
  autoscaler_cooldown_s: 180
  short_backoff_s: 5
```
Leah: Nice. Small standby per AZ buys local capacity without cross-region egress.
Priya: I prefer soft_admit 0.65 canary in us-west-2 only, then measure admitted_rate / reject_rate / p95.
Jorge: I'll run a cost sim for 3 standby nodes/az and post numbers. Need to compare to the cost of 10% static headroom.
Samir: In our sim the p95 drops from ~450ms to ~220ms with the standby buffer, and steady-state cost delta is ~+$Z/day for that region (rough ballpark).
Leah: Also we should instrument warm-delay metric (time between pod ready and first good inference) — currently invisible.
Priya: Agreed — add telemetry and a short-lived histogram bucket for warm-delay so we can correlate with rejects.
Samir: Action items:
- set front_tier.soft_admit=0.65 for us-west-2 canary
- provision 3 standby nodes in AZ-a and AZ-b (tag: standby-spot-preemptible)
- update autoscaler cooldown to 180s for front-tier canary
- add telemetry: admitted_rate, reject_rate, warm_delay_ms, attach_latency_ms
Leah: I'll open the PR for the config change and schedule a canary rollout at 15:00 UTC. tagging @infra-oncall.
autoscale-bot: deploy scheduled by Leah for 2027-09-14 15:00 UTC — canary rollout 10%
Priya: I'll watch the canary, will rollback if reject_rate or p99 latency worsens.
Jorge: Posting cost simulation in a follow-up comment by EOD.
Samir: Thanks all. Marking thread as action-required and adding post-mortem checklist in the canary doc.
